import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Identify the relevant columns
education_expenditure_col = 'Adjusted savings: education expenditure (percentage of GNI)'
gni_per_capita_col = 'GNI per capita (constant 2015 US dollar)'

# Filter the rows for the relevant series names
education_rows = df[df['Series Name'] == education_expenditure_col]
gni_rows = df[df['Series Name'] == gni_per_capita_col]

# Reshape the data to long format
education_long = education_rows.melt(id_vars=['Country Group', 'Country Code', 'Series Name', 'Series Code'], 
                                      var_name='Year', 
                                      value_name='Education_Expenditure')
gni_long = gni_rows.melt(id_vars=['Country Group', 'Country Code', 'Series Name', 'Series Code'], 
                         var_name='Year', 
                         value_name='GNI_per_Capita')

# Merge the two datasets on Country Code and Year
merged_data = pd.merge(education_long, gni_long, on=['Country Code', 'Year'])

# Drop rows with missing values
merged_data = merged_data.dropna()

# Calculate the correlation coefficient
correlation = merged_data['Education_Expenditure'].corr(merged_data['GNI_per_Capita'])
correlation

# Check the data types of the relevant columns
merged_data.dtypes
